stages.label: no-editorial-approvals
stages.explanation: A formal review and management credential do not satisfy the per-write editorial quorum.

stages.label: one-principal-two-credentials
stages.explanation: Two credentials for the same principal count as one reviewer per write.

stages.label: code-missing-second-reviewer
stages.explanation: The document has two reviewers; code still lacks its own second approval.

stages.label: all-writes-approved
stages.explanation: Every write has two distinct active principals; this is an observation, not acceptance.

stages.label: request-changes-veto
stages.explanation: The latest request_changes replaces the earlier approval and blocks acceptance.

stages.label: veto-explicitly-replaced
stages.explanation: Only a replacement naming the current decision clears this principal's veto.

stages.label: reviewer-revoked
stages.explanation: Revocation invalidates this grant's former approvals before acceptance.

stages.label: regrant-does-not-resurrect-decisions
stages.explanation: A new credential for the same principal does not reactivate old grant-bound decisions.

stages.label: fresh-regranted-decisions
stages.explanation: New decisions explicitly pin the new grant and the current policy generation.

stages.label: policy-generation-changed
stages.explanation: A new policy generation invalidates old-generation decisions even when its fields are equal.

stages.label: fresh-current-generation
stages.explanation: Both reviewers recorded new decisions against policy generation 2.

stages.label: accepted
stages.explanation: Authorization, quorum, latest decisions and old runtime guards are checked inside acceptance.

stages.label: authorized-historical-receipt
stages.explanation: A revoked coordinator cannot replay; a newly authorized one receives the original accepted revision.

stages.label: old-runtime-guards-preserved
stages.explanation: Fresh approvals cannot override the competing candidate's stale document read.

limitations: The database owner remains trusted and can bypass the Python API by changing local files.
A credential proves possession of a local capability, not a person's identity, SSO, model identity or expertise.
Distinct principal IDs do not establish independent people, models, evidence or organizations.
Author task names remain self-declared; capability principals authorize reviewer and coordinator operations only.
All decisions are programmed examples; no human review or external LLM call is claimed.
The fictional document and code are stored data; the code is parsed by existing formal guards but never executed.
The policy covers every explicit write; it does not find missing promises, prove natural-language truth or enforce semantic reports.
Public snapshots are sequential observations, not a common transaction; Store.accept is the atomic authorization boundary.
The worker pool size is configuration, not measured throughput or service capacity.
Credential files and the database stay private; published example artifacts contain no bearer secret or credential hash.
